tweets.text:
How do toxic leaders get so far? How did they "make it to where they are?"

1/n
They effectively silence critics (using their authority, influence, etc.)

This can be overt: they make them leave.

Or it can be covert: making critics feel "difficult" and "not a team player".

2/n
They are masters of timing.

They sense when a situation can be exploited. And exit when sticking around will not be advantageous to their reputation.

High profile. Lay low. High profile. Lay low.

3/n
They surround themselves with a buffer of believers...

...people who deflect threats and maintain an alternate reality bubble. They make it structurally difficult to fire the toxic leader, but structurally easy to deflect blame.

4/n
They generate results (but do it at the expense of others).

This becomes their "style", which makes them "rough around the edges, but they get things done".

5/n
They exude confidence in ways that exploit the insecurities of their peers.

E.g. It can be very hard to admit you made a hiring mistake. They exploit this. They nurture narratives that link THEIR success to the success of their peers. And failures to failures.

6/n
They operate at levels of seniority that leave them needing to only influence a small number of people (while explicitly controlling -- through their rank/role -- a large number of people).

Helped by #10 below.

7/n
They keep people guessing through a lot of 1:1 social engineering (both with their reports, and their peers).

No one is able to piece together the big picture.

Lots of "It sucks, but I just can't figure out ....."

8/n
They've mastered leadership platitudes like "We've got to focus" and "We have to keep our eyes on the prize".

These apple-pie statements keep people adjacent to the situation nodding.

"Maybe those naysayers just don't get it"

9/n
When joining, they effectively undermine the prior work of the current team, and then paint themselves as the path to redemption (for the current team).

"You had the right intent, but just needed some direction". "You all worked so hard, but you needed some direction".

10/n
They build their "track record" in dysfunctional environments. No one knows they were dysfunctional! And people don't really do background checks. Plus all the other factors in this thread...

11/n
They cultivate a "survivors narrative".

Basically, they spin a story that "surviving" a stint with their leadership will somehow advance their career, and that it is better to just grin and bear it.

They have examples of this from past orgs too!

12/n
They promote very "all or nothing" type plans.

By getting people to commit to big plans, they create a situation where ppl are left saying "but we'll need to see if this works out first, right?"

13/n

Ultimately, they figure out how to prevent otherwise well-meaning people from taking action through a variety of social engineering techniques.

What have you seen?

...oh, final thought and observation

One of the symptoms is that they make people very unsure of their assessment. Instead of trusting their gut, people spin themselves up over this.

So ... if you feel yourself spun up ... that's a signal as well
